text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's Defence ministry was expected to launch an anti-corruption operation in the country's armed forces, Defence minister Georgi Ananiev said. @

-- A proposal to raise untaxable monthly income to 50,000 levs from current 23,000 levs in line with soaring inflation in the first quarter has been submitted for approval to the new parliament elected on April 19, a deputy from the Alliance for National Salvation said.
-- Only 0.6 percent of Bulgarians polled by the National Statistisc Institute (NSI) considered themselves wealthy, the NSI said. @

-- The Supervisory board of Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had approved the sale of 47 percent of Plovdiv-based cosmetics maker Alen Mak to Varna-based Kanotrans company for $18.3 million. The deal has yet to be approved by the government.
-- Bulgaria expects to receive over $1 billion from privatisation deals this year, a Privatisation Agency senior official said.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 40 billion levs in April to 330 billion levs, Finance Ministry figures showed.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank cut its main interest rate to 5.2 percent monthly from 6.2 percent, to be effective from Monday.
-- Bulgaria expects to choose buyers for two state owned cement makers -- Zlatna Panega and Granitoid-Batanovtsi by May 11, a Construction ministry official said. @
Bulgarian-Spanish consortium Marvex signed an agreement with Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency this week to buy 70 percent of Devnya Cement for $44.5 million.

-- Bulgaria's new parliament voted a declaration on the principles for leading the country out of the crisis, supporting pledges to the International Monetary Fund for introduction of a fixed exchange rate system and implementation of structural reforms.
-- Bulgaria's interim government said it had decided to raise pensions by 16 percent from June. @

-- Bulgaria hopes to reschedule some 680 million Ecus of debt to two banks of the former communist trading bloc Comecon - the International Investment Bank and the International Bank for Economic Cooperation, Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said on return from Moscow.

-- Shareholders of private Elitbank, in receivership since September, decided to raise the bank's capital to 36 billion levs from four billion levs through a new share issue, a bank sequestrator said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
